messages:
alex: thinking about how we map quota tiers -> enforcement semantics for Free / Pro / Enterprise. two main knobs I want us to decide: (1) per-key vs per-org accounting, (2) burst credit model vs strict leaky-bucket. goal: predictable UX and clear console signals for users, and simple runtime enforcement for infra. thoughts? :thinking:

maria: +1 need to pick one canonical source of truth for billing vs enforcement. Currently billing is org-level but many embeds use per-api-key. mixing causes double-counting and weird spikes.

sam: prefer per-org for enforcement, per-key for telemetry. enforcement at org boundary lets us implement throttling and fair-share for teams, while keys can be used for developer-level analytics.

ajeny: (typo) jenny: agree with sam. also want to ensure free tier gets more restrictive burst policy. proposal: Free: tiny burst (100 reqs/5m), Pro: moderate burst (1k reqs/5m) with refill credits, Enterprise: virtually unlimited burst but subject to negotiated SLA and reserve pool.

kevin: important to decide algorithm: token-bucket with refill vs sliding window. token-bucket easier to support burst credits and to show remaining tokens in console. sliding window simpler to reason about but bad UX for sudden ramps.

maria: console UX: show three things per org/key: current usage (tokens used), available burst credits, and time-to-refill. Also surface predicted throttle ETA if current rate continues.

alex: runtime concerns: we have multi-region routing and want to allow burst credits to be consumed across regions but not doubled. do we centralize the credit ledger (consistency overhead) or use local estimation + reconciliation?

sam: prefer local fast-path + eventual reconciliation. i.e., allow local nodes to serve bursts up to local reserve, but maintain a global counter that can clamp for sustained overuse. implement soft-throttle warnings first, then hard enforce.

jenny: telemetry signals we need for ops and product: per-org qps, tail-latency under throttling, number of soft-throttles -> hard-throttles, top keys that hit limits, and costs saved by caching/prefix-eviction. add tags for rollout policy used.

kevin: for routing policies during capacity constraints, prefer policy priority: Enterprise > Pro paid fast-path > Pro best-effort (burst-protected) > Free. fallbacks: model variant downgrade, queueing with ETA, or 429 with human-readable guidance.

maria: UX for developers: when returning 429 include `x-rw-quota-remaining` and `x-rw-quota-reset` headers and an endpoint that returns current quota state. also surface in console alerts and per-route heatmap.

alex: sounds good. open questions: (A) exact refill math for credits (linear vs exponential), (B) enforcement window size (60s vs 5m), (C) acceptable reconciliation lag for global ledger. propose we prototype token-bucket with 5m burst window and 60s rolling enforce. quick experiment would show behavioral differences.

sam: ok to prototype. i'll spike local-ledger + periodic global reconcile. can we add a non-blocking analytics stream for soft-throttle events to product?

jenny: i'll add the telemetry fields to the spec and wire up a dashboard mock. putting suggested PromQLs in that doc.

ops-bot: deploy notice: canary for quota-enforcer spike branch deployed to us-west-2 on canary pool at 1790123478 - watch `quota.enforcer.canary` metric.

kevin: once canary looks good, we need rollout UX: gradual enable by org cohort with a fail-open flag for 24h. product should be able to flip on/off per-org from console.

alex: next steps: sam spike this week, jenny dashboard mock by EOD Fri, maria to draft console headers/UX copy, kevin to write routing priority doc. we'll sync Fri 10am. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
